physical.description: General perception of physical well-being, energy, and bodily function

bands.80:
Scores in this range are commonly associated with patterns such as:
You generally feel physically capable, resilient, and supported in your body. Energy levels, recovery, and day-to-day functioning feel stable.

Self-efficacy impact:
Strong confidence in your ability to maintain and influence physical health.

Ways to strengthen further:
• Continue reinforcing habits that support energy and recovery
• Track subtle signals (fatigue, stiffness) before they escalate
• Use this stability as a foundation for performance or longevity goals
bands.40:
Scores in this range are commonly associated with patterns such as:
Your physical health is functional but inconsistent. You may feel well at times, with periodic dips in energy, stamina, or comfort.

Self-efficacy impact:
You know improvement is possible but may feel unsure where to focus.

Ways to improve:
• Identify patterns (sleep, nutrition, stress, movement) that affect how you feel
• Make small, targeted adjustments rather than broad changes
• Reinforce progress by tracking improvements, not just symptoms
bands.0:
Scores in this range are commonly associated with patterns such as:
You may experience frequent fatigue, discomfort, or limitations that affect daily life.

Self-efficacy impact:
Confidence in the body’s reliability or ability to improve may feel reduced.

Ways to improve:
• Focus first on stabilization (rest, nourishment, consistency)
• Avoid “all-or-nothing” thinking around physical health
• Rebuild trust in the body through gentle, repeatable actions

• Balance intensity with recovery
• Vary movement types to support joints and nervous system
• Use movement as regulation, not just exercise

• Shift focus from “exercise” to “daily movement”

• Anchor movement to existing routines

Self-efficacy impact:

Ways to improve:
• Start with very small, achievable movement goals
• Emphasize circulation and mobility over performance
• Pair movement with energy-restoring practices, not depletion
